matt: heads-up — spotted a regression on qwen2.5 after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. p95 increased ~10-12% on multilingual workloads, p99 spikes more often on zh/jp long sequences.
anya: any quick repro or numbers? which change do you think triggered it?
matt: seems correlated with the new kernel choice that prefers fused qkv matmul (v2) for >64 kv_head_dim. For some qwen2.5 variants we have kv_head_dim=64 but the selector mis-classified due to rounding in compute_shape(). Kernel picked v2, produced slightly different memory layout for KV cache => more memcpy churn and cache misses. Quick profiler snippet below (from local perf run):
```
perf summary (commit abc123 -> abc125):
- kernel_select: qkv_matmul_kernel_v2 used for layer 8-28
- memcpy_device_host: +1.8ms per request (median)
- KV cache hit rate: 99.6% -> 90.8% for zh_longset
- batching efficiency: drop from 0.72 -> 0.63 (adaptive batching)
```
lina: also saw tokenizer edge cases: qwen2.5 tokenizer splits some CJK punctuation differently after tokenizer update; that changes prefix lengths and increases cache eviction frequency for long dialogues. combined effect looks additive.
kevin: sounds like two things: (1) kernel selector mis-detect, (2) tokenizer tokenization boundary shift. I can push a minimal kernel-selector guard: prefer v1 if kv_head_dim == 64 and model_name contains "qwen2". patch is trivial. Also suggest adding a telemetry flag to record kernel_version used per request.
matt: ran a quick local A/B with selector reverted for affected models: p95 back to baseline, p99 reduced ~30%. Numbers: commit abc123 (baseline) p95=48ms p99=210ms; after selector->v2 p95=53ms p99=275ms; revert patch p95=49ms p99=215ms. Will attach microbench harness later.
anya: good. For tokenizer: can we run tokenization diffs on our multilingual corpus and create a small eval set that triggers worst-case caching? if we can reproduce deterministically we can add to the Optimize checks.
kevin: yes — I'll add a small script to bin/ that compares token offsets across tokenizer versions and emits sequences where prefix boundary shifts. use: `python tools/tokenizer_diff.py --model qwen2.5 --corpus corpora/multi_zh_jp.jsonl`.
perf-bot: benchmark job 2026-03-17T14:02:22Z completed: commit abc125 (with v2 selector) — qwen2.5 multi_zh_jp: p50=22ms p95=53ms p99=287ms throughput -8%.
matt: action items: (1) kevin to submit kernel-selector guard + unit tests, (2) lina to produce tokenizer-diff corpus and link failing sequences, (3) anya to run canary with telemetry for kernel choices, (4) add perf test that exercises long CJK prefixes for future regressions. I'll open a short PR tracking all this and attach the perf traces.
anya: thanks — please also include a link to the perf flamegraphs and the exact docker image used for reproducibility. :thumbsup:
matt: will do. quick note — avoid broad revert of batching heuristics; it's the kernel+tokenizer synergy that magnified the issue.
kevin: PR incoming in ~30m. tests: `pytest tests/runtime/test_kernel_selector.py::test_qwen2_kvhead_guard`.
perf-bot: allocated canary in us-west-2 with telemetry flag rt.kernel_version=true. collecting first 1k requests now.
matt: cool, ping here when canary results are in.
